title.rendered: Elohim, the God Who Creates: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
In the beginning, Elohim spoke and the universe answered. Every name of God we will study this week starts here, with the God who creates out of nothing.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, August 11, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”
Genesis 1:1 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

This week, Gospelbuzz begins a new devotional series: the Names of God. Where the last series traced what the believer has been given — authority, righteousness, the keys of the kingdom — this series traces who gave it. Every gift in scripture flows from a name, and every name reveals a facet of the Giver’s character. We begin at the beginning, with Elohim.

The Hebrew word Elohim is plural in form but singular in use throughout Genesis 1, a grammar scholars call the “plural of majesty.” It is the language of fullness — a God whose power is not partial, whose strength needs no reinforcement, who required no raw material to build a universe. Elohim did not organise what already existed. He spoke, and there was.

The Amplified Bible renders it this way: “In the beginning God (Elohim) created [by forming from nothing] the heavens and the earth.” (Genesis 1:1 AMP). That phrase, “from nothing,” is the whole point. Before Elohim, there was no substance to shape. After Elohim spoke, there was light, land, sea, sky, and every living thing arranged with staggering precision.

This matters for more than theology. Whatever feels formless and empty in your life right now — a stalled dream, a broken relationship, a body that will not cooperate, a bank account that will not stretch — is not outside Elohim’s competence. The God who made something out of nothing has never once needed you to supply the raw material. He only ever needed you to receive His word over the situation, the way the darkness received light and did not argue with it.

Over the next ten days we will walk through the names by which God revealed Himself to His people at their point of need: Provider, Healer, Banner, Peace, Shepherd, Righteousness, Almighty, and finally the intimate cry of a child to a Father. But every one of those names rests on this first one. Before He is Jehovah Jireh to the man with empty hands, He is Elohim, the God who can create what does not yet exist.

Prayer

Father, You are Elohim, the God who creates from nothing. I bring You the empty and formless places in my life today — the things that look like darkness over the deep. Speak Your word over them. Where there is lack, let there be provision. Where there is confusion, let there be order. Where there is nothing, let there be something, because You are able. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Elohim, the Creator. He needs no raw material to work with, only my faith to receive His word. What looks empty to me is not empty to Him. He speaks, and it is so.
